title: Portraits of Things: Paintings by Gioia Fonda and Charlie Gill
location: Pence Gallery, 212 D Street, Davis, CA 95616
description:
Portraits of Things: Paintings by Gioia Fonda and Charlie Gill at Pence Gallery in Davis 
Exhibit: October 9 – November 29, 2026 
Reception: Friday, October 9, 6-9 PM (Free) 
Artist Talk: Sunday, November 8, 2-3:30 PM (Free) 
  
Interdisciplinary artist Gioia Fonda has long collected colorful toys, both for their intrinsic charm and as creative inspiration. As a student at California College of the Arts, she arranged small collectibles into still-life compositions, captured them on film, and processed the photos at a local drugstore. Captivated by these arrangements, her advisor, Charlie Gill, painted spare compositions based on her photographs—works that now hang alongside hers. For this exhibition, Fonda has created a series of new paintings featuring similar arrangements of toys and found objects. She is also offering an opportunity for members of the public to exhibit their own small works on paper, riffing on some of her recent photos. Artists may add to this display throughout the duration of the show.  
  
Sponsored by the Pence Community Curatorial Fund. 
  
Image: Gioia Fonda, “Holding It Together”

title: 2nd Friday ArtAbout at the Pence Gallery
location: Pence Gallery, 212 D Street, Davis, CA 95616
description:
Join us at the Pence Gallery in Davis for our 2nd Friday ArtAbout reception on October 9, 6-9 PM. Enjoy browsing all new exhibits, complimentary wine, and an art-themed scavenger hunt. Free admission! 
  
Portraits of Things: Paintings by Gioia Fonda and Charlie Gill | Oct. 9 – Nov. 29, 2026 
This series features Gioia Fonda’s new paintings of arrangements of toys and found objects, alongside paintings by her advisor Charlie Gill based on her past still-life photographs. 
  
Mercy Hawkins: Waltz of Life & Limb | Oct. 3 – Nov. 6, 2026  
Pairing her sculptural paintings and vibrant, large-scale watercolors on paper, Mercy Hawkins’ biomorphic shapes speak to a sensory play of color, light, and movement. Her imagery evokes seed pods, flower buds, or microscopic creatures.  
  
Danilo Campos: Out and About | Oct. 9 – Nov. 29, 2026 
Danilo Campos’ paintings explore his love of new places and experiences, reflecting his way of seeming to mindlessly go ‘out and about,’ but coming back with gems of resources. 
  
Misuk Goltz’s Class: Expressive Watercolor | Oct. 2 – Nov. 15, 2026 
This stairway show illustrates what Misuk Goltz’s watercolor students have achieved during the course of her workshops and reflects the community of painting, encouragement, and friendship that she has fostered while teaching at the Pence since 2020.  
  
Scavenger Hunt: Join us for a fun, art-themed scavenger hunt at the Pence during the 2nd Friday ArtAbout. Complete all of the clues by exploring our exhibits for the chance to win a special prize.

title: Anton Barbeau Album Release Concert Live @ The Melon Ball
location: The Melon Ball – Watermelon Music, 1970 Lake Blvd., Davis, CA, 95616, United States
description:
Live music at the Melon Ball in Davis. 
October 9th is the release date for Anton Barbeau’s latest album, Come Home To Me.  The record features performances from Colin Moulding and Dave Gregory (XTC) as well as Andy Metcalfe, Donald Ross Skinner and Terry Edwards. 
Anton is pleased to bring his All Time Xmas Band to the Melon Ball to launch the album. Watch out Steinway! 
Anton Barbeau, a Sacramento native and lifelong songwriter, has released nearly 40 albums, including his latest, Come Home To Me, a joint release between Gare du Nord (UK), Rock Indiana (Spain) and Think Like A Key (USA). After 2025’s “Dad death, DMT and Steely Dan” trilogy, Come Home To Me is a *somewhat* more straightforward affair, with clean, jangly pop songs like “World Calls Love” and the title track demanding attention. Still, there’s always room for musical mischief on an Anton album, as the floppy P-Funk of “I Touched The Butter” demonstrates. 
Barbeau has worked with members of XTC, Cake, The Pretenders, The Soft Boys and the Bevis Frond. In Sacramento, the local newspaper might struggle to spell his name correctly, but in England, Stewart Lee stands in the front row at his gigs. Popmatters says of him, simply, “Anton Barbeau is one of the best unknown pop singer-songwriters in the world, period.” After living abroad for 15 years, first in the UK and then in Berlin, Barbeau has returned to California, and now lives on his wife’s small town family farm.

title: Jim Bruno’s Songwriting Workshop
location: Watermelon Music, 1970 Lake Blvd, DAVIS, CA, 95616, United States
description:
Jim Bruno Workshop in Davis. 
Jim Bruno is a San Francisco Bay Area based published songwriter. He taught Songwriting at the Freight and Salvage in Berkeley and at Foothill College in Los Altos Hills both for 11 years. 
He’s also taught Songwriting Workshops at Chicago’s Old Town School of Folk Music, at Far-West Music Conference, at San Francisco State University’s High Sierra Campus and more. 
Songs he’s written have been recorded and released by Shawn Colvin, Chuck Prophet, Mary Lou Lord, Cliff Eberhardt, Thad Cockrell, Maurice Tani and Laurie MacAlister. 
As a performing songwriter he has performed with or opened shows for the following artists: Shawn Colvin, Timothy B Schmidt of the Eagles, Graham Parker, John Gorka, Charlie Musselwhite, Joe Ely, Greg Brown, Steve Forbert, Bill Morrissey, Big Twist, and Cliff Eberhardt.  He’s performed at the Greenwich Village Folk Festival, the Udine Folk Festival in Udine, Italy and has toured five times in Europe. He also played bass, guitar and sang in the Shawn Colvin Band for several years and often performed with Shawn as a duet. 
He has signed numerous song publishing agreements including Largo Music in New York and Bug Music in Los Angeles. 
Enrollment is $20
Participants are asked to bring a printed lyric sheet to the event

Written by acclaimed Sacramento-based director-playwright Anthony D’Juan, Superior California is a work of historical fiction inspired by the life of Mr. Campbell, bringing to light a powerful, lesser-known chapter of regional history.

description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering
Update 8/14/25:
**We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)

We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.

People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.

Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.

You're not required to buy anything in order to join us, but we do encourage you to support local businesses. Blue Note's chef team makes a mean pizza, and there are other nearby downtown restaurants and businesses.

We hold self-guided figure drawing sessions with a nude model every 2nd & 4th Wednesday of the month, from 6:30–9 PM. title: Imagining America National Gathering
description:
Join over 500 participants from the IA network and the University of California, Davis and Yolo Bioregion community (a geographic and cultural area that includes the cities of Davis, Woodland, Winters, West Sacramento, and surrounding areas) to engage in deep learning, collaboration, and transformative creativity on the theme of Tides of Transition: Restoring Collective Spirit in Troubled Times. We will activate spaces across the UC Davis campus, in the City of Davis, and at community-hosted site visits. 
Tides of Transition: Restoring Collective Spirit in Troubled Times calls us to re-story and honor the places, knowledges, relationships, and ecologies that have been made broken through centuries of violence and abandonment, and the current intensifying fear and repression. We know that our communities are tired, and we know that being together revives our collective spirit, giving us the strength and inspiration we need in troubled times. In this moment of upheaval, the 2026 IA National Gathering draws participants to Davis, CA in the spirit of mending the roots of our connections, and to “awaken,” as Buddhist monk and activist Thích Nhất Hạnh teaches, “from the illusion of our separateness.”

location: Pence Gallery, 212 D Street, Davis, CA 95616
description:

Art in Action engages kids in art projects that are fun, creative, and collaborative with their family members. This is a drop-in program for ages 5-12.
